# ngwr

> Angular UI library — standalone, signals-first, zoneless, fully tree-shakable.
> 166 secondary entry points, 181 component and directive classes, built on
> `@angular/cdk` primitives. The only runtime dependency is `tslib`. Docs and
> live demos: https://ngwr.dev — source: https://github.com/thekhegay/ngwr

This file orients AI agents and LLMs that consume ngwr. For exact, current
component APIs, read the bundled TypeScript types
(`node_modules/ngwr/types/ngwr-<name>.d.ts`). ngwr.dev is prerendered, so
fetching a route returns real HTML you can read; the machine-readable resources
listed at the bottom are still the faster path for bulk API lookups.

## Install

Preferred — the schematic installs ngwr + its peers, adds `@use 'ngwr'` to your
global styles, and prints a tailored provider snippet to paste into bootstrap:

```
ng add ngwr
```

Or add it manually (pnpm / npm / yarn):

```
pnpm add ngwr @angular/cdk
```

Requires Angular / CDK `>= 22.0.0` (peers: `@angular/cdk`, `@angular/common`,
`@angular/core`, `@angular/platform-browser`, `rxjs ^7`; optional `date-fns` /
`luxon` / `lucide`).

Each component is a tree-shakable subpath import: `import { WrButton } from
'ngwr/button'`. Styles: `@use 'ngwr'` (everything) or `@use 'ngwr/<name>'` (per
component) in your global SCSS.

## Providers (main.ts)

Add from their entry points as needed:

- `provideWrOverlay()` — strongly recommended for any overlay (dialog / select /
  dropdown / popover / toast / drawer): gives ngwr its own CDK overlay container
  so it never collides with other CDK consumers, and installs the visual-viewport
  tracker mobile sheets need to clear the on-screen keyboard. Without it overlays
  still work, falling back to CDK's shared root container — but
  `--wr-keyboard-inset` stays 0 and sheets won't lift above the keyboard. Add
  `provideWrResponsiveOverlays()` for mobile sheets.
- `provideWrIcons(lucideIcons({ check: Check }))` — icon registry (`ngwr/icon`,
  adapters under `ngwr/icon/adapters/*`).
- `provideWrTheme()` — `--wr-*` design tokens. `provideWrDensity()` — sizing.
- `provideWrConfig({ button: { size: 'sm' }, select: { rounded: true } })`
  (`ngwr/config`) — app-wide component DEFAULTS. A value bound on the element always
  wins, and a bound `false` beats a configured `true`, so a config never has to be
  escaped. Covers `size` on the form controls, `rounded` on `input` / `inputNumber`
  / `select`, and `linkTarget` / `copyable` on `markdown`. There is deliberately no
  `color` key — a bound `[color]="null"` means "no intent", which a default cannot
  express without inventing a sentinel.
- `provideWrI18n(...)` + `provideWrI18nStaticLoader(...)` — localization.
- `provideWrDateAdapter(...)` — calendar + date-picker (`ngwr/date-adapter-fns`
  or `ngwr/date-adapter-luxon`).

Injected rather than provided: `WrTour` (`ngwr/tour`) runs a guided onboarding
tour — `tour.start([{ target: '[data-tour="save"]', content: '…' }])` spotlights
one element at a time; a step whose target is missing is skipped, not floated.

## Schematics — let `ng` wire it

- `ng add ngwr` — installs peers, adds `@use 'ngwr'` to styles, prints provider setup.
- `ng g ngwr:use WrFoo --path src/app/x.ts` — adds the import + splices `WrFoo` into that
  component's `@Component` imports.
- `ng g ngwr:provider <overlay|icons|toast|i18n|date-adapter|density|theme|…>` —
  adds the matching `provideWr*()` to bootstrap.
- `ng g ngwr:icon-set` — scaffolds a tree-shaken icon barrel.
- `ng g ngwr:component-style <name>` — appends `@use 'ngwr/<name>'` (opt-in styles).
- `ng g ngwr:page <form|table|dashboard>` — starter page wired with ngwr.
- `ng update ngwr` — runs upgrade migrations.

## Use ngwr — don't hand-roll

The catalog is large: prefer an ngwr component, util, pipe, or validator over raw
markup, custom logic, or another library. e.g. use `wr-file-upload`, not a bare
`<input type="file">`; reach for `ngwr/utils`, `ngwr/pipes`, `ngwr/validators`
before writing your own. Full catalog: https://ngwr.dev/reference/components.

## Common components (selector — import)

- **Form** — `wr-btn` (ngwr/button), `wrInput` (ngwr/input), `wr-select`
  (ngwr/select; modes single/multi/search/tag, plus `searchable` for a
  multi-with-typeahead and `(searchChange)` for server-side search),
  `wr-checkbox` (form state is `[(checked)]`; inside `<wr-checkbox-group>` the
  identity input is `checkboxValue`, NOT `value`), `wr-switch`, `wr-slider`,
  `wr-input-number`, `wr-input-otp`, `wr-date-picker` (date/time/datetime) and
  `wr-date-range-picker` (both in ngwr/date-picker; the range value is
  `[start, end]`, hence a separate component), `wr-file-upload`,
  `wr-form-field` (in ngwr/form), `wr-color-picker`, `wr-transfer` (dual listbox;
  the value is the RIGHT pane).
- **Data** — `wr-table` (column pin/resize/drag-reorder, row selection,
  expandable rows, grouping, tree rows (`childrenKey`), summary rows,
  CSV export, virtualized body),
  `wr-pagination`, `wr-tree`, `wr-virtual-scroll`, `wr-sortable-list`
  (drag-to-reorder, with `[wrDragHandle]` — both in ngwr/drag-drop).
- **Feedback** — `wr-alert`, `wr-result`, `wr-empty`, `wr-skeleton`,
  `wr-spinner`.
- **Layout / Display** — `wr-card`, `wr-carousel`, `wr-collapse`, `wr-splitter`,
  `wr-toolbar`, `wr-descriptions`, `wr-statistic`, `wr-lightbox`,
  `wr-pull-to-refresh`, `wr-markdown` (renders markdown as DOM, never as HTML —
  raw HTML in the source is escaped; `[streaming]` for a partial document;
  `provideWrMarkdownHighlighter()` takes coloured spans, not markup).
- **Navigation** — `wr-tabs`, `wr-stepper`, `wr-breadcrumbs`, `wr-dropdown-menu`
  (with its `[wrDropdown]` trigger — both in ngwr/dropdown).
- **Overlays** — `wr-drawer` (or `WrDrawerManager.open()` to open a component as
  a drawer from code), `wr-action-sheet`, `[wrPopover]` (directive; has a
  `tooltip` mode), `wr-command-palette`, `wr-context-menu`, `wr-popconfirm`.
  (Dialog and toast are service-opened — inject `WrDialog` / `WrToast`.
  Content inside a service-opened dialog or drawer can `inject(WrDialogRef)` /
  `inject(WrDrawerRef)` to close itself.)

## Patterns

- **Forms** — every value control is signal-forms native (`FormValueControl`, or
  `FormCheckboxControl` for checkbox) — no `ControlValueAccessor` in between.
  Bind `[formField]="form.x"`, use the two-way model standalone (`[(value)]`, or
  `[(checked)]` on checkbox/switch), or classic `[(ngModel)]` / reactive forms
  via Angular's bridge.
- **Icons** — register via `provideWrIcons`, render `<wr-icon name="check" />`.
- **i18n** — `{{ 'key' | wrT }}` (pipe from `ngwr/i18n`).
- **Theme** — CSS custom properties `--wr-color-*`, `--wr-border-radius-*`, … set
  by `provideWrTheme()`. Two contrast tokens per intent, easy to confuse:
  `--wr-color-<intent>-contrast` is the label ON a filled intent;
  `--wr-color-<intent>-ink` is the intent used AS text on a surface or its own
  `-soft` tint. A bare `--wr-color-<intent>` as text clears AA on a plain light
  surface for every intent but `warning` and `light`, but still fails on the `-soft`
  tint — which is exactly where outlined / ghost / tinted variants paint it, so use
  `-ink` there. For muted prose use `--wr-color-on-surface-muted`, not the `medium`
  intent.
- **Mobile** — overlays collapse to sheets (`provideWrResponsiveOverlays()`), a
  `responsive` input reflows layout components, a `touch` density preset enlarges
  controls, and `WrHaptics` (ngwr/platform) fires vibration feedback.
- **Large datasets** — `virtualScroll` is an opt-in input on `wr-table`,
  `wr-tree` and `wr-select` (search mode), alongside the standalone
  `wr-virtual-scroll` wrapper.
- **Testing** — CDK component harnesses ship beside the components they drive, at
  `ngwr/<name>/testing`. 36 entry points so far, 65 harness classes, covering the
  form controls, the overlays, both data views, the navigation / disclosure set
  (`tabs`, `stepper`, `carousel`, `pagination`, `segmented`, `collapse`,
  `transfer`) and `markdown`: the form controls
  (`button`, `input`, `textarea`, `checkbox`, `switch`, `radio`, `select`,
  `input-number`, `input-otp`, `slider`, `rating`, `file-upload`, `color-picker`,
  `form` for `<wr-form-field>`), the overlays (`date-picker`, `dropdown`,
  `popover`, `dialog`, `drawer`, `action-sheet`, `toast`, `context-menu`, `popconfirm`,
  `command-palette`, `cascader`, `mention`) and the data views (`table`, `tree`) —
  every control and overlay entry point has one.
  Load them with `TestbedHarnessEnvironment` and narrow with
  `WrButtonHarness.with({ text: 'Save' })` instead of querying ngwr's markup.
  Dialog, toast and a service-opened drawer render outside the fixture — load
  those from `documentRootLoader()`; everything else is an element in your
  template, and where its panel is in the overlay the harness reaches it for you,
  scoped to that instance by the id the trigger publishes.
  Many are families: `WrTableHarness` + row / cell / header-cell, `WrTreeHarness`
  + node, `WrCascaderHarness` + column / option, `WrCommandPaletteHarness` +
  group / item, `WrRadioGroupHarness` + radio, `WrSliderHarness` + thumb,
  `WrInputOtpHarness` + box, `WrRatingHarness` + item, `WrContextMenuHarness` +
  item (submenus included), `WrMentionHarness` + option, `WrTransferHarness` +
  pane / item, `WrMarkdownHarness` + code block.
  A unit test has no layout, so anything a mouse would drag (slider, rating,
  file-upload's drop zone) is driven by the KEYBOARD or by real events, never by
  coordinates. Guide: https://ngwr.dev/guides/testing
- **Scheduling** — `wr-event-calendar` covers month / week / day in one
  component. `events` is an input the calendar never writes to: a drag emits
  `eventChange` with the proposed start / end, and you apply it. Event `end` is
  EXCLUSIVE. `editable` turns on drag and resize; `Alt` + arrows do the same
  from the keyboard.

## Resources (machine-readable)

- This quick-ref: https://ngwr.dev/llms.txt
- Full reference (every entry point + selector + description):
  https://ngwr.dev/llms-full.txt
- **One page as markdown — append `.md` to any docs URL.**
  `https://ngwr.dev/reference/components/select` also serves
  `https://ngwr.dev/reference/components/select.md`: the same page as markdown,
  prose and code samples and API tables, without the site chrome. Prefer it over
  `llms-full.txt` when you already know which component you need. Each HTML page
  advertises its twin as `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`.
- **MCP server — the same files, askable.** `npx -y ngwr-mcp` (a bin in the
  installed package; zero dependencies, JSON-RPC over stdio) exposes four tools:
  `search_ngwr` turns a need into an entry point name, `get_ngwr_component`
  summarises one entry point, `get_ngwr_api` returns a class's inputs / models /
  outputs read out of the shipped `.d.ts`, and `get_ngwr_setup` returns the
  install / `ng g ngwr:use` / provider commands as text — it never runs them,
  and it never reaches outside its own package: no network, no commands. It reads the resources
  listed here rather than embedding a copy of them. Client config for Claude
  Code / Claude Desktop / Cursor, and a worked example of each tool:
  https://ngwr.dev/guides/mcp
- All site URLs (for crawlers): https://ngwr.dev/sitemap.xml
- Source, README, per-component `.d.ts` types: https://github.com/thekhegay/ngwr
  (installed at `node_modules/ngwr/types/ngwr-<name>.d.ts`; the package also
  ships `README.md`, `llms.txt`, and `llms-full.txt`)
